body: All coverage in Madagascar was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera.
Several boat trekkers can be found throughout the country.
Most coverage features one or several people walking alongside the trekker, helping to recognize the country.
Madagascar has two official languages: French and Malagasy, written with the Latin alphabet.
The climate of Madagascar varies from extremely dry in the south and central parts to tropical in the north.
The coverage in Ambanja is recognizable by a person wearing a dark blue T-shirt and black sunglasses.
Coverage on Nosy Ambariovato features several people with distinct clothing in a hilly, forested area.
There is a village by the northern shore of Nosy Ambariovato.
Ambiky is recognized by many palms and a brown, sandy dirt road.
A beach west of Ambiky features low trees and low mountains to the northwest.
An area south of Ambiky has large solitary green bushes and a slight red tinge in the dirt.
Coverage along the Sambirano river shows a person wearing a dark blue T-shirt and sunglasses.
A small section of the Sambirano river coverage includes two different people with distinctive clothing.
A couple of atolls on the central west coast appear on Street View, with the northern one consisting only of sand.
Other atolls feature broad leaved palms, which are rare in Madagascar.
Most coverage in Antananarivo is from the side of a hill looking over the city towards the Queens Palace.
Coverage on RN8 shows a silver roof rack on the Street View car in a dry, sandy environment.
The trekker on RN8 includes four people wearing red, blue, grey, and light blue.
Baobab Avenue is notable for its broad-trunked baobab trees along the road.
Morondava is recognized by a bald person wearing a light green or light red striped shirt and by streets paved with road.
Morondava has a smooth sand beach with large numbers of palms and the ocean to the northwest.
Belo Sur Mer features many palms combined with a blanket of white sand on the ground.
The beach outside Belo Sur Mer is recognizable by dirty sand and a curved shoreline with the ocean to the northwest.
Kirindy Mitea National Park has the reddest soil present on Street View in Madagascar.
A car with a barely visible grey metal roof rack is seen by Manahy; some locations are blurred out.
Coverage partly taken on a large grassy field and partly on the side of sand dunes is south of Manahy.
A village with the shore to the east is found north of Andavadoaka.
A small, very sandy village with the shore to the north can be seen on a small cape north of Andavadoaka.
The town of Andavadoaka has three different people appearing on the coverage.
The main trekker coverage in Andavadoaka shows a person wearing a greyish hat and light blue shirt or a yellow T-shirt.
A second trekker going northeast of Andavadoaka can be recognized by a person with a light blue T-shirt.
A blue cart dragged by a black cow on the left and a brown-white cow on the right is found south of Andavadoaka.
Another cart dragged by a white cow on the left and a black and white cow on the right can be found just south of Andavadoaka.
A small seaside village with no visible people can be found in the northern end of the bay south of Andavadoaka.
Coverage on a somewhat rocky ground with no people following the trekker is southwest of the bay.
Coverage includes multiple people walking near the trekker and a small village to the west in the southeast bay.
A cluster of fishing nets can be found in the bay.
The first of two parts located in the town of St Augustin.
The second part with two people is east of St Augustin, passing through a hilly landscape with shrubs.
A row boat with five people and a wide wooden frame is northwest of Ambohimena.
A boat going up the Sambirano River shows two people, a tourist with a blue T-shirt and a gondolier.
A small part of Tsaranoro coverage was taken inside a forest, sometimes hiding mountains.
A boat covering small atolls along the central west coast is recognizable by the driver with a white cap and no shirt.
The Tsaranoro Massif, a large monolithic mountain, has trekker coverage.
Toliara is a busy town and the only large town with no person following the trekker.
Steep mountainsides and a mountainous area make St Augustin coverage very recognizable, with people following the trekker.
